localBiteReport: The fall transition is well underway around Choctawhatchee Bay and the Destin area, and the inshore bite is reportedly among the best of the year according to local guides. Capt. Adam Schroeder of Ignite The Bite Charters (Destin) notes that bait is now easy to locate in the mornings, with redfish, flounder, trout, and mangrove snapper all actively responding. Redfish around bridges are responding well to live croakers and spot minnows, while the overall pattern is shifting from the sluggish mid-summer heat toward more consistent early-fall feeding windows. The most recent Choctawhatchee Bay-specific report (week of Sept 4–10) from Capt. Blake Nelson with Last Cast Charters confirmed sight-fishing redfish opportunities are improving as bait schools push from open water onto flats and into bayous. Water temperature is 85°F. Note: the Great Days Outdoors report covering Sept 25–Oct 1 focused primarily on offshore grouper fishing and did not include updated Destin inshore specifics; the Sept 18–24 report is the most current with detailed inshore bay content.
